World Bank (1996). China: Efficient Industrial Boilers. GEF Project Document, Report No. 16132-CHA, The World Bank, Global Environment Coordination Division, Environment Department, Washington DC, November 1996.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). Project appraisal document for a GEF grant to improve nine coal-fired industrial boiler models in China. Loaded: for each of the nine subprojects the existing-model and improved-model thermal efficiency (Annex 7 output indicators: baseline 1995 vs target at 100% and 60% load), boiler market price in thousand CNY (Annex 10 Table 5: current average and improved = current x (1 + printed % premium), computed) expressed per t/h of steam, the size of the reference boiler (Annex 9 Table 2 case list), the price survey (Table 4, 4 and 10 t/h) and the stock-average efficiency (60-65%) and service life (15 years). Measures file: efficiency gain as coal saving per unit heat (derived 1 - eta_old/eta_new), price premium and consumer payback. Not loaded: incremental-cost totals (discounted, in other-values), emission-reduction tables, technical assistance costs, producer economics. Traps: no price year printed (publication year 1996 used; exchange rate 8.5 CNY/USD for 1995); Annex 5 Table 1 consumer payback (3.95-5.26 y) differs from Annex 9 Table 2 "with project" payback (4.6-7.8 y); the subproject 1 part-load target is garbled in the PDF ("78/6%") and not loaded; boiler sizes are from the cost-benefit case list, not the model ranges (1-100 t/h); efficiencies are thermal efficiency with no heating-value basis printed (Chinese practice normally LHV). The existing-model and improved-model examples both map to the same archetype.
